thread.title: 7 Best Ways To Gauge How The Stock Market Is Doing

author: NANCY GONDO
title: 7 Best Ways To Gauge How The Stock Market Is Doing
text:
Whether you have your heart set on Apple ( AAPL ) or Facebook ( FB ), Alibaba ( BABA ) or Baidu ( BIDU ), or a domestic vs. foreign stock, here's good news.
X You don't have to pick just one of them. You could buy both stocks. Or, you could buy shares of an exchange traded fund, which offers a simple, low cost and tax efficient way to invest. It also lowers individual-stock risk, since you're buying a basket of stocks. ETFs trade just like stocks.
Today there are some 2,000 ETFs to choose from across a wide range of categories that cover stocks, bonds, commodities and currencies. And you can further slice and dice based on your preferences, whether you favor growth or value, small-cap or midcap, tech or health care, or a specific country or region.
Below are some key index funds often used as a barometer to find out what's going on in the stock market for some of those segments.

Please contact customer service CLOSE Let's start with one of the most widely used bellwethers to track Wall Street's health: the Dow Jones industrial average. The Dow is a price-weighted average of 30 blue chip stocks such as Apple, Boeing ( BA ), Caterpillar ( CAT ), General Electric ( GE ) and McDonald's ( MCD ). Many of these are your grandfather's stocks — they have a large market cap, are actively traded and tend to generate steady earnings growth.
SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ( DIA ) with $21.4 billion in assets For a broader sampling of the market, there's the S&P 500 Index, composed of 500 of the biggest U.S. companies trading on the NYSE or Nasdaq.
SPDR S&P 500 ( SPY ), $261.7 billion If tech stocks are more your flavor, check out the Nasdaq 100 Index, which tracks the 100 stocks with largest market capitalization listed on the Nasdaq, excluding financials. This index is topped by Apple, Amazon.com ( AMZN ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), Facebook and Alphabet ( GOOGL ).
PowerShares QQQ Trust ( QQQ ) $63.4 billion For midcap and small-cap segments of the market, here are two commonly watched funds:
